$description: Provisional code names for the Figma semantic colour tokens. This file is the single place to rename: keys are Figma names (property/group/role), values the name used in code (class = name with / replaced by -, CSS variable = --guk-<class>). Several Figma names may map to one code name only when their Light and Dark values are identical (the generator checks). Every Figma name not listed keeps its name. `additions` are code-only tokens that Figma does not define as semantic variables yet. An addition either has its own `light`/`dark` values or is an `alias` of another token (same value in every theme, unless `semantic-colors.parity.json` gives it a default-theme override: then it holds that value in the default theme and follows the aliased token in "next" and "dark", a component-level alias, P-51). `utilities` declares the utility families generated beside the one-per-token utilities (see its own description).

utilities.$description: Extra utility families, generated for every token of the named families (Tailwind emits only the classes a source uses). Naming (P-41): single-side borders keep Tailwind's grammar, the side replacing the family (`border-t-accent-secondary` applies border/accent/secondary to the top side); every other applier is followed by the full token class (`from-gradient-surface-primary`, `fill-bg-surface-tertiary-inverse`, `caret-text-surface-secondary`), so the Figma token name stays readable in the class. Fades: `<gradient token>-to-<direction>` paints a gradient token to its `-transparent` twin (the semantic counterpart of the kit's `gradient-neutral-50-transparent-to-b`). `alphaStops` are the few stops that need a fixed opacity of a token, named like Tailwind's opacity modifier. `crossFamily` applies a token to a property of another family where the designer bound it so; each entry is a provisional decision (P-42) with its reason.

alphaStops.note: The collapsible's overflow fade has a 70 % middle stop today (via-neutral-0/70); Figma draws it with two stops (gradient/surface/secondary-transparent > secondary). Kept as today (O-01); the middle stop is listed for the designer.

crossFamily.note: Switch thumb, unchecked and checked + disabled: Figma fills the handle with icon/surface/secondary (G-17). Same colour today (neutral-300).
Switch thumb, checked: Figma fills the handle with icon/accent/primary (G-17). Same colour today (primary-400).
Progress threshold marker outline: Figma strokes it with bg/surface/primary, the card surface the marker is cut out of (G-17). Same colour today (neutral-0).

ProposalVotingProgress container in a row: the items keep their 1px bottom border, painted in the card's own surface colour to hide it (today border-b-neutral-0 on a neutral-0 card). Code-only: Figma has no bottom divider in the row layout.

Text-input caret: Figma draws it as a fill bound to bg/surface/secondary-inverse in every input focus state (G-07, G-17); the data-list filter's caret binds text/surface/secondary instead (G-18). Each follows its binding (P-28).
Tab trigger underline: Figma draws it as a border bound to border/surface/selected; the code draws it with a box-shadow, so the token is applied as the shadow colour. Same colour today (primary-400).

primitiveRemap.$description: Palette-change preview (L-01) in the "next" value set only: every primitive colour variable (--color-<ramp>-<step>, the variables behind the primitive classes such as bg-neutral-50 and text-critical-600) is redeclared under [data-theme="next"] as the same step of the corresponding Figma ramp, so markup that still uses primitive classes follows the new palette in "next". The ramp correspondence is the one of `semantic-colors.parity.json` `fallbackRamps`, read in reverse (neutral -> gray, primary -> aragon, success -> green, warning -> orange, critical -> red, info -> blue). A step the Figma ramp lacks takes the nearest one; `steps` decides the ties (the generator fails on an undecided tie). The default theme and "dark" are not touched; dark is not remapped on purpose (P-55). Not a semantic conversion: the classes keep their step, only the palette under them changes (P-54).
